To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rap1 prevents NHEJ between wild‐type telomeres in S. cerevisiae.

1) telomere fissions in rap1Δ cells are dependent on NHEJ factors, 2) the frequency of fission is not affected by the absence of Sae2 and Tel1 and 3) fission occurs between telomeres that are of near wild‐typelength.
Rap1 is required for the suppression of NHEJ between the telomeres in S. cerevisiae.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the suppression of telomere fusion by Rap1.
how cells protect their chromosomes from fusion.
the mechanisms that prevent telomere fissions and telomere fuses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Rap1 prevents fusions by NHEJ.
Rap1 prevents telomeres from fusing by NHEJ.
Rap1 is a universal inhibitor of NHEJ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rap1 prevents telomeric end fusions by inhibiting NHEJ.
Rap1 is an evolutionarily conserved factor that prevents NHEJ at telomeres.
Rap1 prevents telomeric fusions via NHEJ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Rap1 has a second function in addition to telomere protection: it suppresses NHEJ.
the presence of Rap 1 at telomere prevents telomere end fusions by NHEJ.
the Rap1‐dependent suppression of NHEJ is essential to prevent telomere fusing.
